findings.statement: CXCR2 ranks first in the convergence ranking: up in UC biopsies (meta log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814]) and with an Open Targets association score of [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345]. It has expression, replication, inflammation, genetics, literature and tractability streams, and clinical-stage antagonists in other indications (reparixin at late clinical stage; navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682 at mid stage), but it has no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL, so MR is not tested.

CXCR2 has a substantial mouse colitis literature (a CXCR2 antagonist is reported to ameliorate acute experimental colitis), but MGI holds no curated single-gene colitis phenotype, so the direction rests on literature titles only. Safety: no curated safety events, not flagged as strongly constrained, and no pleiotropic traits share its genetic signal.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in UC biopsies and the plasma pQTL MR is significant with higher protein lowering UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), colocalising with an IBD GWAS signal and replicating in FinnGen (OR [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=0.734]). Because the protective direction is for higher protein, PD-L1 blockade (checkpoint antibodies exist) would be expected to worsen, not treat, UC; the gene is a protective-axis marker, not an inhibition target. No gut eQTL instrument.

The CD274 MR sensitivity analysis is mixed: Steiger direction is correct and the Egger intercept is not significant, but heterogeneity across the three instruments is nominally significant. No known safety events; the gene is not flagged as strongly constrained. Mouse colitis papers exist but MGI has no curated phenotype.

IL12B is the strongest MR hit and an established UC drug target: higher plasma protein raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=IL12B; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.539]), it colocalises with the IBD GWAS and replicates in FinnGen and a second UC GWAS, so inhibition is the protective direction. It tops the Open Targets UC list but is not among the top convergence-ranked biopsy genes, so it is a genetics-led rather than expression-led target. No gut eQTL instrument.

CXCL8 is a strongly induced neutrophil chemokine (meta log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.864]) with only anti-IL-8 antibodies at mid clinical stage, but it has no Open Targets genetic support and plasma MR is null (p [gene=CXCL8; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; p=0.289]), with no FinnGen replication: a strong expression change without genetic causal support, best treated as a biomarker.

CXCL5 is up in biopsies, but plasma MR shows higher protein lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]), replicating in FinnGen and a second UC GWAS, using a tag variant and without IBD GWAS colocalisation. The direction is opposite to the pro-inflammatory expression change and argues against inhibiting this chemokine; the lack of colocalisation weakens it. No gut instrument, so blood and gut cannot be compared.

IDO1 is strongly and consistently induced (meta log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.118]) and has clinical-stage inhibitors (linrodostat late stage, epacadostat at approval stage in the record) in other indications, but has no Open Targets genetic association; mouse colitis papers exist with mixed titles (epithelial and immune-regulatory roles) and no curated MGI direction.

JAK2 has the second highest Open Targets UC association ([gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318]) and approved or clinical inhibitors, yet its biopsy change is modest compared with the effector genes, and it has no cis-pQTL instrument, so MR is not tested. Genetic support is not matched by a large expression change.

AQP9 is among the most induced genes (meta log2FC [gene=AQP9; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.075]) in all cohorts, but it has no drug and no genetic association, and tractability is only predicted; CHI3L1 shows the same pattern, and CXCL1, DUOX2 and S100A8/A9 are similar: strong neutrophil-linked biomarkers without genetic support.

FCGR2A combines a high Open Targets genetic score with a modest biopsy increase and no drug; FCGR2B plasma MR is significant with higher protein raising UC risk and IBD GWAS colocalisation, pointing to Fc-gamma receptor signalling as a genetics-supported mechanism that is weakly visible in expression.
SLC26A3 is down in UC biopsies with genetic association in Open Targets and no drug; the epithelial transport loss accompanies mucosal inflammation, and no MR estimate was retrieved for it.

In the gut layer, IRF8 expression in GTEx transverse colon raises UC risk and colocalises with the IBD GWAS, as does a LINC01475 locus signal; the top gut hits are mostly non-druggable regulatory loci and do not overlap the top biopsy-expression genes, so blood, gut and expression layers largely point to different genes.

caveats: Not tested in MR means no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL, not evidence against a gene (CXCR2, JAK2 not tested).
Plasma protein is not mucosal protein; gut eQTL instruments existed for few candidates.
Drugs listed are as returned by Open Targets for any indication, not UC efficacy.
Mouse evidence for CXCR2, IDO1 and CD274 is literature presence only; MGI has no curated colitis phenotype for them.
Tool-call budget limited coverage; STRING and UniProt were not queried.
